recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Further source edits would be redundant and could create drift between the Condition narrative notes and StructureDefinition comments; revisit only if Patient Care changes the broader Condition onset/abatement choice-type model.
issue_request: FHIR-7618 was a Published Patient Care change request with resolution Persuasive with Modification. It asked to clarify when/how Range should be used for Condition.range / Condition.abatement, and the accepted resolution was to explain that Range communicates the subject's age at the time of abatement.
initial_application: The issue appears to have been applied by git commit b8fddd3c068912bd2981dbdc86f25090047c11ce, whose message explicitly references #7618 and added a Condition.abatementRange usage note to source/condition/condition-notes.xml. The note was later editorially refined but continues to say that Range communicates an imprecise age at abatement.
additional_context: Condition is active in source/fhir.ini, so the source/condition files checked are in current build scope. Later Applied issue FHIR-50437 revisited Condition.onsetRange and Condition.abatementRange and added matching Range guidance to Condition.abatement[x] comments in source/condition/structuredefinition-Condition.xml. FHIR-12064 separately rejected removing distinct abatement choice types. Direct Zulip and Confluence searches for FHIR-7618 found no conflicting community record.
reconciliation: No source change was made. source/condition/condition-notes.xml already has a Use of Condition.abatementRange section stating that Range communicates an imprecise age of the subject at abatement, and source/condition/structuredefinition-Condition.xml now also distinguishes Period as imprecise abatement timing from Range as an imprecise age range.

related_jiras.note: Later Applied issue clarified Condition.onsetRange and Condition.abatementRange comments and confirms the current wording.
